# Paths that must trigger a build and a test run.
#
# THE RULE: changing this list requires saying in the pull request what stops being covered.
#
# This file is a committed contract, not documentation. `.github/scripts/assert-build-affecting-paths.py`
# reads it, reads the `paths:` filter on `.github/workflows/dotnet-build.yml`, and fails the build when a
# path listed here is not covered by any pattern in that filter. Narrowing the filter for speed is what
# this exists to make visible: on 2026-04-17 the trigger was scoped to `.cs`/`.csproj` (47a82ad45), and on
# 2026-08-05 a `Directory.Packages.props` dependency bump - described in its own pull request as the
# riskiest change in the repository - merged with no build at all (c9fbc8d99), because a change confined
# to that file matched none of the remaining patterns. Benchmarks broke while landing green for the same
# reason (51590103c).
#
# FORMAT: one entry per line. Either a literal repository-relative path, or a directory followed by `/**`.
# Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. Every entry is verified to exist in the repository, so the
# list cannot rot into fiction. Each entry carries the evidence for why it is here - add nothing on taste.

# Every compiled and packaged artifact. Deliberately the whole tree and not `Source/**/*.cs`: the
# `.proto` contracts under `Source/Kernel/Protobuf` generate the C# the kernel and every client compile
# against, and `Source/**/*.props` and `.json` files change how projects build, none of which an
# extension-scoped filter reaches.
Source/**

# The out-of-process integration suite the build workflow hands its cache and image to.
Integration/**

# The build workflow builds both benchmark projects. Without this a broken benchmark project lands green
# and fails on the next unrelated pull request instead - which is exactly what happened in 51590103c.
Benchmarks/**

# The build workflow runs `docker build -f Docker/Local/Dockerfile .` and the out-of-process integration
# jobs consume the image it produces, so a Dockerfile or entrypoint change decides whether they can run
# at all. A Docker exec-bit fix once could not cut a release because the publish trigger did not list
# this (fd48b6471).
Docker/**

# Central package management decides what every project in the repository compiles against, so a version
# bump here reaches further than any single project file.
Directory.Packages.props

# Imported by Directory.Packages.props for the net8.0 and net9.0 target frameworks. The build workflow
# builds the client packages for every shipped framework, so these decide what those builds resolve.
Directory.Packages.NET8.props
Directory.Packages.NET9.props

# Sets the properties the whole build runs under, including EnforceCodeStyleInBuild.
Directory.Build.props

# Filters which `.globalconfig` Roslyn resolves. Get this wrong and analyzer severities across the
# repository change without a single source file being touched.
Directory.Build.targets

# Pins the SDK the entire build runs on.
global.json

# Analyzer severities under warnings-as-errors - roughly 150 and 80 entries respectively. A severity
# change here turns the build red or green on its own.
.globalconfig
.editorconfig

# A project added to or dropped from the solution changes what gets built and what gets tested, without
# necessarily touching a single source file. The solution-membership assertion reads it.
Chronicle.slnx

# Passed to `dotnet test --settings` for the specs run, so it decides how the specs execute.
specs.runsettings

# The workflow definitions themselves - including the one this contract constrains. A change here is
# precisely the class of change that silently removes coverage.
.github/workflows/**

# Scripts the build and integration workflows invoke directly: assert-solution-membership.py,
# collect-coverage.sh, generate-integration-matrix.py, run-tests-with-retry.sh.
.github/scripts/**

# This file. Editing the contract has to re-run the check that enforces it.
.github/build-affecting-paths.txt
